memorial_details: A wooden cross with attached dedicatory laminated label, the left arm of the cross has the silhouette of a Lancaster and the right a Hurricane; also a wooden board mounted on a metal shaft with a dedicatory plaque. Both are placed within a black propeller shaped kerbing filled with black stones, the tips of the propeller shape and their stones are painted yellow.
narrative: On March 11, 1945, Lancaster bomber LM130 of 463 Squadron, based in Lincolnshire, was involved in a tragic mid-air collision near Blankney. The exact circumstances of the accident remain unclear, but it resulted in a catastrophic loss of life. This incident marks a somber reminder of the risks faced by aircrews during World War II, underscoring the sacrifice made by these brave individuals in service to their country.
